cars.variant: Trans Am hardtop 335-hp 400 Ram Air — 1969 USA production launch, three-speed manual
cars.specification_market: 1969 USA Firebird Trans Am hardtop, standard 335-hp 400 Ram Air V8 and heavy-duty three-speed manual, using the production launch advertisement with the matching AMA Firebird 400 H.O. engine row. Count the original 1967–1969 Firebird performance-road family once across years, engines, bodies and packages. Retain period factory Ram Air/400 H.O. nomenclature rather than treating later Ram Air III shorthand as a separate identity. Not a 303 racing engine, Ram Air IV prototype, GTO-rated engine or second-generation car. Advertised native power only; no modern net conversion, prototype test times, mass or production count inferred.
cars.summary: The first Trans Am established a defining Pontiac performance identity within the original Firebird family, combining Ram Air V8 power with a purposeful handling package and distinctive functional bodywork. First-hand interviews with Pontiac development participants document its creation and lasting recognition, distinguishing the production road car from experimental racing programmes.

sources.notes: Six-page file, 14,018,307 bytes. Full PDF index 4 visually read: actual Trans Am launch advertisement, with standard 335-hp 400 Ram Air, heavy-duty three-speed, 3.55 axle, fiberglass-belted tyres, heavy-duty springs/shocks, one-inch bar, power front discs and variable-ratio power steering. Index 5 also viewed but shows ordinary GTO/Firebird imagery and supplies no selected fields. Other pages rendered, not individually viewed. No unlisted front spoiler or specific tyre size imported.

sources.source_type: Original manufacturer AMA specification sheets, hosted scan
sources.notes: 33-page file, 12,759,384 bytes. Full indexes 0, 2 and 3 visually read; other rendered pages not individually audited. Cover identifies hardtop body 22337. Power-team table on printed page 3 distinguishes 330-hp Firebird 400, selected 335-hp 400 H.O. and 345-hp Ram Air IV. Detailed engine values map only to the matching 335-hp row; the later launch advertisement controls Trans Am package equipment and axle ratio. No base-model chassis assumptions or GTO engine ratings.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The first Trans Am established a defining Pontiac performance identity within the original Firebird family, combining Ram Air V8 power with a purposeful handling package and distinctive functional bodywork. First-hand interviews with Pontiac development participants document its creation and lasting recognition, distinguishing the production road car from experimental racing programmes.

media.caption: 1969 Firebird Trans Am hardtop photographed by Matt Morgan; white-and-blue body, twin scoops, fender louvres and rear spoiler shown. Representative exterior photograph only: modern BFGoodrich Radial T/A tyres are visible and do not represent the factory fiberglass-belted fitment. The image does not authenticate engine tune, gearbox, brakes, factory package identity or restoration originality; the title’s Polar White wording is not adopted as a factory paint-code claim.
